rationale: The correct float->i1 lowering is LSB(trunc_toward_zero(a)). I replaced each buggy (i1 (fp_to_*int fXX)) -> (SETP_iNNri $a, 0, CmpEQ) pattern with a two-step composition that reuses already-defined, well-tested nodes: (1) convert the float to a 32-bit integer with round-toward-zero via CVT_{s,u}32_fXX $a, CvtRZI — the exact same instruction nodes the adjacent i32 (fp_to_{s,u}int fXX) patterns already use; then (2) extract the low bit via SETP_i32ri (AND_b32ri ..., 1), 0, CmpNE — the same idiom the existing i1 (trunc i32) pattern at line 2209 uses. The composition equals LSB(trunc_toward_zero(a)), exactly what the x86 oracle emits (cvttss2si followed by a low-bit extract: movzbl for unsigned, andl $1 for signed). Signed vs unsigned CVT is preserved per-pattern; they differ only when the truncated value is outside {0,1}/{0,-1}, where the result is poison anyway, so AND-with-1 low-bit selection is correct for all defined inputs. I used 32-bit CVT/AND/SETP for all source types (including f16/bf16 and f64) for uniformity and because PTX integer regs are naturally >=32 bits; this matches how the existing i32 conversion patterns are written. I deliberately did not add a doF32FTZ variant for the i1 f32 case to keep the change minimal and consistent with the prior (non-FTZ) i1 pattern; the FTZ-only difference for subnormals cannot change the i1 result since the low bit of a truncated subnormal (magnitude <1) is 0 either way. Verified all eight CVT_{s,u}32_fXX nodes already exist and are used elsewhere in the file.
general_case_safe: Only the i1 result-type patterns are changed; the i16/i32/i64 fp_to_sint/fp_to_uint patterns (the common case) are untouched and still use CVT_{s,u}NN_fXX directly. Each replacement references CVT/AND/SETP instruction nodes that already exist and are exercised by surrounding patterns (verified each CVT_{s,u}32_fXX already appears in the file), so no new instruction defs are needed. The new lowering produces LSB(trunc_toward_zero(a)) — matching x86 — for every defined input across f16/bf16/f32/f64, signed and unsigned, and yields a defined-but-unspecified low bit only where LangRef already permits poison (truncated value not in {0,1}/{0,-1}). No other type or conversion path is affected.

rationale: The narrow-type multiplier 1<<ShiftAmt is only safe for MUL_WIDE_SIGNED if it is non-negative in FromVT, because mul.wide.s sign-extends its operands. The only failing case is the top-bit shift (ShiftAmt == FromVT.bits-1), where MulVal.isNegative() is true. Bailing out (returning SDValue()) leaves the SIGN_EXTEND/SHL node for normal type-legalization and ISel, which lowers sext(shl x, k) as a sign-extending load + shl (matching what x86 emits: shll $15 then movswl), producing the correct sign. I scoped the guard to (a) the SHL branch only, so plain MUL widening is untouched, and (b) Opcode == MUL_WIDE_SIGNED, so the ZERO_EXTEND/MUL_WIDE_UNSIGNED path (where the narrow constant is zero-extended and 0x8000 correctly means +32768) is unaffected. Verified the buggy llc emits mul.wide.s16 %rs,-32768 / mul.wide.s32 %r,-2147483648 for the repro, and the x86 oracle emits shll+movswl/movslq i.e. the positive-shift-then-sign-extend semantics my fallback yields. Cannot rebuild per instructions, but the combine's SDValue() return is the standard no-op path and requires no other changes.
general_case_safe: Non-top-bit signed shifts (e.g. shl i16 x,14 -> 1<<14=0x4000) remain non-negative in FromVT, so isNegative() is false and they still combine to mul.wide.s16 x,16384 as before. The plain MUL widening case is outside the if(SHL) block and entirely unchanged. The zero-extend/MUL_WIDE_UNSIGNED path is excluded by the Opcode==MUL_WIDE_SIGNED guard, so zext(shl x,15) still folds to mul.wide.u16 x,0x8000 (correctly +32768 under unsigned widening). The only behavior change is for the single broken case (signed widening of a top-bit shift), which now falls back to the correct generic lowering instead of producing a sign-flipped product.

rationale: Root cause: the clamp's 32-bit amount (ShiftOp.getOperand(1), the truncated value) can disagree with the guard's full-width ShiftAmt about the predicate `amount < BitWidth` when ShiftAmt has nonzero high bits above bit 31. The fix gates the rewrite on those dropped high bits being provably zero. I compute ClampAmt = ShiftOp.getOperand(1) (the value that actually feeds the PTX clamp, always i32 per the SHIFT multiclass `(OpNode t.Ty:$a, i32:$b)` in NVPTXInstrInfo.td). If ShiftAmt is wider than ClampAmt and computeKnownBits(ShiftAmt).countMaxActiveBits() exceeds the clamp width, the truncation is lossy and the combine bails (returning SDValue() leaves the correct guarded selp/setp expansion in place). Verified against ISel DAG dumps: for the buggy i64 repro, setcc binds ShiftAmt = t6 (i64) while the shift amount is `t10: i32 = truncate t6`, so 64 > 32 and an unknown i64 param has countMaxActiveBits()==64 > 32 -> combine correctly suppressed. When the high bits are known zero (e.g. amount = zext i32), countMaxActiveBits() <= 32 and the combine still fires. KnownBits.h is already #included and computeKnownBits is used elsewhere in this file.
general_case_safe: The common cases are unaffected. (1) i32 guarded shifts: ShiftAmt and ClampAmt are the same i32 node (ShiftAmt.getValueSizeInBits()==ClampAmtBits==32), so the `>` check is false and the combine fires exactly as before. (2) i16 guarded shifts that are currently optimized: confirmed via ISel dump that after legalization setcc binds ShiftAmt = t20 (i32) and the shift amount operand is the same t20 (i32) -- both 32 bits, so the new check is skipped and `shr.u16` is still emitted. (3) i8 cases were already not folded (guard constant mismatch) and are untouched. (4) i64 amounts with provably-zero high bits (e.g. zext from i32) still fold because countMaxActiveBits() <= 32. Only the genuinely-unsound case -- ShiftAmt strictly wider than the 32-bit clamp amount with unknown/nonzero high bits -- is blocked, and there the compiler falls back to the correct guarded selp expansion (a clean correct path, not a wrong result or a crash).

rationale:
Root cause: LowerINT_TO_FP (NVPTXISelLowering.cpp) lowered `int -> bf16` as `int -RN-> f32` then `FP_ROUND f32 -RN-> bf16`, two roundings. For i32/i64 the int->f32 step is itself lossy, so the f32 intermediate can land on a bf16 tie and the second rounding diverges from the correctly-rounded direct result (witness 33685505).

Fix: make the int->f32 step round-to-odd (the Boldo/Melquiond "double rounding is odd" construction the sibling LowerFP_ROUND already uses for f64->bf16). Round-to-odd at the intermediate guarantees the subsequent single round-to-nearest f32->bf16 (`cvt.rn.bf16.f32`, still legal/unchanged) is correctly rounded. Implementation, for i32/i64 only: compute F32 = int->f32 (round-to-nearest); convert it back to int (exact, since F32 is integral here) and compare with the source to detect inexactness; determine rounding direction by |int| vs |back|; nudge the f32 bit pattern by +1 (toward larger magnitude) or -1 (smaller) to the odd neighbor, but keep F32 untouched when the conversion was exact or F32 is already odd. This mirrors TargetLowering::expandRoundInexactToOdd exactly, adapted to an integer source (no wider exact FP exists for i64, so the FP-operand helper can't be reused directly).

Why DAG combine doesn't defeat it: DAGCombiner::FoldIntToFPToInt only folds FP_TO_S/UINT(S/UINT_TO_FP(x)) -> x when f32's 24-bit precision >= the effective input size; for i32 (eff. 31/32) and i64 (63/64) it refuses, so the exactness SETCC is preserved.

FP_TO_SINT/UINT, SINT/UINT_TO_FP, ABS (Expand for i32/i64), BITCAST, ADD, AND, SETCC, SELECT are all legal/legalizable on NVPTX. getSetCCResultType returns i1 for all scalars here, so the OR of the two booleans is type-consistent.

Edge cases verified: x=0 and powers-of-two (incl. signed INT_MIN, where ABS overflows to itself) are exactly representable in f32 -> Exact short-circuits, so the ABS poison is never selected. Inexact inputs are never INT_MIN, so ABS is well-defined there. Negative values handled via raw-bit +/-1 matching the abs-based direction (same as expandRoundInexactToOdd).

Follow-up (not part of this edit): add a regression function to llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/bf16-instructions.ll (or convert-sm80.ll) for sitofp/uitofp i32/i64 -> bfloat.
general_case_safe: i1/i16 sources are excluded from the new code (the `if (IntVT == MVT::i32 || IntVT == MVT::i64)` guard), so those convert via the unchanged single-rounding path — they always fit exactly in f32, so there is no double rounding and no added cost. For i32/i64, when the int->f32 conversion is exact or already odd (the common case for small/representable values), `Keep` is true and F32 is returned bit-for-bit unchanged, so only inexact-and-even intermediates are nudged — exactly the values that previously mis-rounded. The final f32->bf16 step is still the same legal `cvt.rn.bf16.f32` (LowerFP_ROUND returns Op unchanged for an f32 source on sm_80+), and FP_TO_INT(INT_TO_FP) is provably not folded away by DAGCombiner for i32/i64 (precision check fails). The STRICT_* opcodes are not routed here (only SINT_TO_FP/UINT_TO_FP are set Custom), so Signed detection via opcode is exhaustive. Non-bf16 result types are untouched.

rationale: Root cause is a missing-visitor (incomplete InstVisitor) class of bug: atomicrmw/cmpxchg are writes through the pointer but ArgUseChecker only overrides visitStoreInst/visitMemTransferInst/visitMemSetInst, so atomic writes silently hit the no-op default and the arg is misclassified read-only. The fix adds the two missing visitors, mirroring visitStoreInst exactly: when the byval arg is the address operand of an atomicrmw/cmpxchg it is a write and we PI.setAborted(...), forcing a per-thread local copy (case 3, copyByValParam: alloca + memcpy from param space, uses redirected to the alloca, no readonly/grid_constant). When the arg is instead used as a value/compare/new-value operand the pointer itself is being stored, so we setEscapedAndAborted(...) just like the store-of-pointer case. The required NVPTX includes (llvm/IR/Instructions.h) are already present, so AtomicRMWInst/AtomicCmpXchgInst are visible. I verified with the built opt/llc that the unpatched pass emits `ptr readonly byval ... "nvvm.grid_constant"` with no alloca and `atom...param...` PTX, while the plain-store sibling correctly takes case 3 (alloca+memcpy). A regression test should be appended to llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/lower-byval-args.ll or lower-args-gridconstant.ll (byval arg written via atomicrmw + select, asserting alloca/memcpy and absence of readonly/grid_constant). I scoped the fix to atomicrmw/cmpxchg (the confirmed repro plus its documented identical sibling); the freeze variant mentioned in round-2 corroboration is a distinct mechanism (missing user-enqueue / pass-through, not a missing abort) and is intentionally out of scope for this minimal fix.
general_case_safe: Read-only byval params still take the existing fast paths: a load through the arg falls through the no-op visitInstruction (verified: load case still becomes ld.param in param AS with no local copy), and visitStoreInst/visitMemTransferInst/visitMemSetInst are unchanged, so case 1 (all-loads -> param AS) and case 2 (genuine grid_constant) are untouched. The new visitors only fire for atomicrmw/cmpxchg. Setting Aborted is the maximally-conservative outcome (full local copy via copyByValParam), which is always correct, so even if an abort fires earlier than a would-be escape the result is sound. Genuine __grid_constant__ params that use atomics still take case 2 via the isParamGridConstant(*Arg) disjunct (mutation of a grid_constant is UB), so their no-copy lowering is preserved. The arg-as-value-operand sub-case mirrors the established store-of-pointer escape handling, so pointer escapes via atomics are not newly missed.

rationale: Root cause is information loss: the generic DAGTypeLegalizer::PromoteIntRes_VAARG promotes an i8/i1 VAARG to RegVT i16 and discards the original type, so by the time NVPTXTargetLowering::LowerVAARG runs it sees VT=i16 and advances/loads at 2 bytes. The NVPTX caller (LowerCall) packs sub-i16 integer varargs at 1-byte stride (st.b8), so caller and callee disagree. A post-promotion fix in LowerVAARG is impossible because original-i8 and original-i16 both arrive as i16 and must use strides 1 and 2 respectively. The only place the original sub-i16 type is still visible is BEFORE promotion. PromoteIntegerResult calls TLI.CustomLowerNode(N, getValueType(0), /*LegalizeResult=*/true) -> ReplaceNodeResults, but only if getOperationAction(ISD::VAARG, i8) == Custom. Edit 1 registers that. Edit 2 handles it in ReplaceNodeResults by reusing the existing LowerVAARG on the un-promoted node (VT=i8/i1): it advances the va_list by getTypeAllocSize(i8)=1 and emits a 1-byte load — exactly matching the caller's st.b8 packing. The returned value is the original (illegal) i8/i1 type, built from non-VAARG nodes (load/add/store), so it is then promoted by the standard load legalization (i8 NON_EXTLOAD -> EXTLOAD i8->i16, which NVPTX selects to ld.local.u8) with no re-entry into VAARG promotion (no loop). i1 reuses NVPTX's existing i1-load custom lowering. After the fix, second_i8 reads offset 1 (where the caller stored %b) instead of offset 2.
general_case_safe: Only MVT::i1 and MVT::i8 VAARG are newly routed to ReplaceNodeResults; these are exactly the types whose register-type promotion (to i16) creates a stride mismatch with the caller's 1-byte packing. i16/i32/i64/ptr/double va_arg are legal (or already correctly sized) results: they never enter PromoteIntegerResult for VAARG, so they continue through the unchanged MVT::Other Custom path into LowerVAARG and advance by their own alloc size (2/4/8), which still matches the caller. The i8/i1 VAARG node is consumed during type legalization, so no i8/i1 VAARG ever reaches the LegalizeDAG action dispatch; the i16 action is untouched. The 2-result (value+chain) contract of ReplaceNodeResults is preserved and the chain is rethreaded by the normal load promotion. The change is confined to lib/Target/NVPTX (no generic or other-target code), so only NVPTX variadic lowering is affected. Verified the committed test variadics-backend.ll and the built llc agree that the caller uses 1-byte stride for i8/i1, which is what the fixed callee now matches.

rationale: The aggregate load/store pair has memmove (overlap-safe) semantics, not memcpy. The fix materializes an llvm.memmove with the load/store's pointers, alignments, length, and combined volatility, then expands it via the existing, well-tested expandMemMoveAsLoop, which for a constant length calls createMemMoveLoopKnownSize. That helper emits a runtime `src < dst` (compare_src_dst) check and copies backward when dst > src, so every destination byte equals the ORIGINAL source byte (dst[i]=src[i]), matching the IR's load-then-store semantics and the NOTES' Expected result (p[8+i]=original p[i]). createMemMoveLoopKnownSize is static in LowerMemIntrinsics.cpp and not exported, so reusing it via a materialized memmove keeps the entire fix inside the NVPTX target. expandMemMoveAsLoop can return false only when src and dst are in different address spaces that NVPTX's TTI reports as may-alias (default true) but with no valid addrspacecast (default false); in that case I fall back to the original createMemCpyLoopKnownSize call so previously-handled cross-address-space aggregate copies still lower to selectable code (and in NVPTX distinct non-generic address spaces don't physically overlap, so a forward copy is correct there). IRBuilder.h is newly included; MemMoveInst comes from the already-included IntrinsicInst.h. The MemCalls (explicit llvm.mem*) path is untouched, so existing lower-aggr-copies tests are unaffected.
general_case_safe: Non-overlapping, same-address-space aggregate load/store (the common case) now lowers via the memmove path, which still copies correctly; it adds only a cheap runtime src<dst branch selecting an equivalent forward loop, the minimum needed since the pass has no alias info to prove non-overlap. Overlapping copies (the bug) now get the correct direction. Cross-address-space aggregate load/store that expandMemMoveAsLoop declines falls back to the exact prior createMemCpyLoopKnownSize lowering, so no regression and code still selects. Volatility is preserved (memmove volatile = LI||SI volatile, conservatively correct). Byte-or-smaller / sub-128-byte aggregates never reach this loop (the >=MaxAggrCopySize=128 guard at line 74 is unchanged). The explicit llvm.mem* intrinsic lowering path is not modified.

rationale: The root cause is a missing fallback handler in ArgUseChecker. Adding a visitInstruction override that calls PI.setAborted(&I) makes any pointer-consuming instruction the checker doesn't specifically handle take the conservative path, exactly mirroring the existing visitMemSetInst handler. With PI aborted, lowerKernelByValParam sets ArgUseIsReadOnly=false: case (1) (convertToParamAS, which crashes) is skipped; case (2) is taken only for grid_constant params (HasCvtaParam && isParamGridConstant), where using the pointer directly is valid; otherwise case (3) creates a correct local copy via copyByValParam. For the repro, this materializes an alloca + memcpy of the byval struct and performs the icmp against the local copy, so the comparison against null is well-defined and %out receives 0. I chose setAborted rather than setEscapedAndAborted to match visitMemSetInst: these instructions use the pointer locally and need a copy but do not necessarily leak it to another function; abort alone already forces the conservative copy.
general_case_safe: InstVisitor always dispatches to the most-derived visit* method matching the concrete instruction type, so load/gep/bitcast/addrspacecast/store/ptrtoint/phi/select/memcpy/memset/call/intrinsic continue to hit their existing specific overrides unchanged. visitInstruction is reached only as the fallthrough for instruction kinds that have no handler — precisely the previously-misclassified set (icmp/freeze/atomicrmw/cmpxchg and any future unconvertible consumer). For those, CloneInstInParamAS would have hit llvm_unreachable anyway, so the read-only fast path (case 1) was never a valid option; routing them to the copy/grid-constant paths is strictly more correct, never a regression. Convertible uses still take case (1); grid_constant params still use the direct pointer via case (2); everything else gets a semantically-correct local copy via case (3).

rationale: The branch condition's intent is "if the vector occupies at least as many bytes as it has elements, each element is byte-or-larger so buffer one element at a time; otherwise the elements are sub-byte and must be packed". The bug is that it used the top-level global's buffer size (aggBuffer->getBufferSize() = AggBuffer::Size) instead of the current vector's own size. The fix replaces it with getDataLayout().getTypeStoreSize(CV->getType()), which is exactly the metric used to size the top-level buffer (printModuleLevelGV line ~1072: DL.getTypeStoreSize(ETy)). getDataLayout() is already an available AsmPrinter member (used elsewhere in this same function/file). BuffSize was used nowhere else, so the rename is complete. For <8 x i4>: getTypeStoreSize = 4 < NumElems = 8 -> packing path -> correct 4 bytes (33,67,101,135) followed by the i32 305419896 little-endian (120,86,52,18), matching the NOTES Expected and the working standalone top-level case.
general_case_safe: Byte-or-larger element vectors are unaffected: getTypeStoreSize >= NumElems holds (e.g. <4 x i32>=16>=4, <2 x i64>=16>=2, <8 x i8>=8>=8), so they take the unchanged "one element at a time" path. The previously-working standalone top-level <8 x i4> is also unchanged: there the old BuffSize was already DL.getTypeStoreSize(ETy)=4, identical to the new VecByteSize=4, so it still takes the packing path and emits the same bytes. Only the broken nested case changes: VecByteSize (the vector's own store size, e.g. 4) is now correctly < NumElems (8), routing to the existing packing code instead of overflowing the buffer. No other code reads getBufferSize() for this decision.

rationale: Root cause: the splat-ConstantInt/ConstantFP branch in bufferAggregateConstant emitted one byte per vector lane, with no sub-byte packing, while the AggBuffer is sized to the vector's store size. For <8 x i4> this writes 8 bytes into a 4-byte buffer (assert/OOB) and would be the wrong layout. The fix detects a sub-byte element type (getPrimitiveSizeInBits() < 8) and packs the (identical) splat lane value into bytes, mirroring the established logic in the sibling bufferAggregateConstVec: NumElemsPerByte = 8/ElemBits, each output byte ORs the lane value shifted into successive sub-byte positions, and the loop runs ceil(NumElems/NumElemsPerByte) times = the buffer's store-size byte count, with the final byte naturally partially filled (remaining buffer bytes stay zero-initialized = correct tail padding). I verified the produced bytes exactly match both the x86 oracle and the existing NVPTX ConstantVector path: <8 x i4> splat 3 -> {51,51,51,51} (0x33 per byte), <8 x i1> splat true -> {255}, <3 x i4> splat 7 -> {119,7} (0x77, then one lane 0x07). Sub-byte FP types do not exist (smallest scalar FP is half=16 bits), so when ElemBits<8 the constant is necessarily a ConstantInt, making cast<ConstantInt> safe. The added assert(8 % ElemBits == 0) matches the identical invariant already asserted in bufferAggregateConstVec, so no behavior regression for the supported i4/i2/i1 cases. general_case_safe: Byte-or-larger element types (ElemBits >= 8) are completely unchanged: they fall through to the original per-lane bufferLEByte loop, so scalar/byte vector splats, ConstantFP splats (half/bfloat/float/double, all >= 16 bits), and all non-sub-byte cases behave exactly as before. The new code only runs for sub-byte integer splats (i4/i2/i1), which previously crashed/miscompiled. The packed-byte count equals the AggBuffer's store-size, so no overflow and no under-fill mismatch with printBytes/printWords (which read the full zero-initialized Size). Output is byte-for-byte identical to the already-correct ConstantVector path (verified against both that path and the x86 oracle), so the flag-on and flag-off representations now agree.

const uint64_t BitWidth = II->getType()->getIntegerBitWidth();
  ConstantRange Range(APInt(BitWidth, Low), APInt(BitWidth, High));

rationale: The crash is purely an APInt construction issue: High is a uint64_t exclusive upper bound that can equal 2^BitWidth, which is not an N-bit value. APInt provides an implicitTrunc parameter (APInt.h:111-113) exactly for this; passing implicitTrunc=true truncates 0x100000000 to 0 in 32 bits. The resulting ConstantRange [1, 0) over i32 is the canonical wrapped representation of the full domain {1..0xffffffff} = [1, 2^32), which matches the NOTES' Expected result (range(i32 1, 0), a saturated range). I confirmed the crash with the buggy opt and confirmed the boundary: maxclusterrank=4294967294 yields range(i32 1, -1) = [1, 0xffffffff). Low is left strict (no implicitTrunc) because a Low >= 2^BitWidth would itself be a genuine bug worth catching; only the exclusive High legitimately reaches 2^BitWidth.
general_case_safe: implicitTrunc only changes behavior when High >= 2^BitWidth; for every High < 2^BitWidth the constructed APInt is bit-for-bit identical to before, so all existing ranges (tid.*, ntid.* capped at 1024/64, cluster_ctaid/nctaid.* capped at 0x7fffffff/0xffff, and nctarank below type-max) are unchanged — verified that maxclusterrank=4294967294 still emits range(i32 1, -1). The only path that can hit High==2^32 is cluster_nctarank, whose MaxClusterSize (=MaxNctaPerCluster) is uncapped; there the wrapped [1,0) range correctly denotes the full i32 domain rather than asserting. No miscompile: the truncated value yields the mathematically correct full-domain ConstantRange, and InstCombine's downstream use of this range remains conservative (a full range constrains nothing).

rationale: The root cause is truncating division `Val.getBitWidth() / 8` as the loop bound in `ExtendBuffer`, which omits the final partial byte for widths that aren't a multiple of 8. The fix uses ceiling division `(bitWidth + 7) / 8` for the byte count and extracts the final byte with only the bits that remain (`min(8, bitWidth - I*8)`), since `extractBitsAsZExtValue` rejects reads past the bit width. This is exactly the technique already used and proven in `bufferLEByte`'s `AddIntToBuffer` (lines 1657-1672) for the nested-large-int path; this just brings the top-level large-int path into line. Hand-verified against the x86 oracle: i65 2^65-1 now emits all 9 bytes {255 x8, 1}, matching x86's `.quad -1; .byte 1`.
general_case_safe: For byte-multiple widths (i64, i128, fp128's 128 bits, i256) the new `NumBytes = ceil(bitWidth/8)` equals the old `bitWidth/8`, and every iteration computes `NumBits = min(8, bitWidth - I*8) = 8`, so behavior is byte-for-byte identical to before — no regression for the common case (i128/fp128 are unchanged). The only changed behavior is for non-byte-multiple widths >64, where one additional final byte is now written with the correct high (bitWidth%8) bits. The subtraction `Val.getBitWidth() - I * 8` cannot underflow: the loop runs I in [0, NumBytes), and NumBytes = ceil(bitWidth/8) guarantees I*8 < bitWidth for every iteration, so the operand stays positive. Both callers of ExtendBuffer (top-level ConstantInt and fp128) are covered correctly.

rationale: Replaced the fragile per-byte sub-vector-bitcast merge with a uniform bit-packing layout: pack every element into a single APInt of width VecByteSize*8, with element I at bit offset I*ElemTySize, then emit VecByteSize little-endian bytes. This matches the LLVM DataLayout vector packing and the x86 oracle: for a <2 x i3> with values 1 and 2 x86 emits .byte 17 (binary 00_010_001) and the new code produces 17. The model reproduces every existing expectation in test/CodeGen/NVPTX/sub-byte-constant-vectors-i4-i2.ll byte-for-byte (test0=33, test1=228, test2=33,67, test3=228,228, test4=1, test5=33,3, test6=33,33,1, test7=228,11, test8=228,228,11), and the non-divisor cases now lower correctly (e.g. <8 x i3> -> 209,88,31; <8 x i5> -> 65,12,82,204,65), all matching x86. The dropped divisor assert was the bug; nothing downstream needs the divisor property because we pack by bit offset rather than whole-byte element groups. Undef/poison elements contribute zero bits (matching old folding behavior), and a non-foldable element still triggers the existing report_fatal_error. insertBits and extractBitsAsZExtValue stay in bounds: max insert end NumElems*ElemTySize <= VecByteSize*8, and byte extraction range fits within VecByteSize*8. Required includes (ADT/APInt.h, IR/Constants.h, Analysis/ConstantFolding.h) are already present. Per instructions I did not build; verified layout against the x86 oracle and existing regression expectations.
general_case_safe: The byte-or-larger element path (VecByteSize >= NumElems) is untouched, so all normal vector globals are unaffected, including the single-element <1 x i4> case that takes that fast path. The rewritten sub-byte path produces byte-identical output to the old code on the divisor cases it already handled (verified against the existing i4/i2 regression test expectations and the x86 oracle), so no existing valid case regresses; it additionally makes the previously-crashing non-divisor sub-byte widths (i3/i5/i6/i7) lower to the same layout x86 produces. Genuinely unlowerable elements still reach the same report_fatal_error as before rather than silently emitting wrong bytes.

rationale: Root cause is canLowerToLDG() admitting atomic loads: isInvariant() is a MemSDNode predicate, so an atomic load with MOInvariant satisfies the LDG guard and reaches tryLDG(), whose else-branch reads operands 3/4 that only exist on NVPTXISD::MLoad, not on a 2-operand AtomicSDNode {chain, ptr}. The minimal, semantically correct fix is to exclude ISD::ATOMIC_LOAD from canLowerToLDG (used by both tryLoad and tryLoadVector). This is also correct on the merits: ld.global.nc (ldg) is a non-atomic load and cannot represent an atomic ordering, so lowering an atomic load to ldg would silently drop the monotonic/acquire ordering — a miscompile. After the exclusion, the atomic load falls through to tryLoad's existing path, which already has an explicit `case ISD::ATOMIC_LOAD` (UsedBytesMask = UINT32_MAX, non-extending) and lowers it as a real atomic global load. Verified the current tool crashes in tryLDG on the repro, and that a non-invariant atomic load with the same triple/cpu already lowers to `ld.relaxed.sys.global.b32` — exactly the output the fixed path will now produce for the invariant case (matches NOTES' Expected). The opcode check matches the switch-on-opcode style used elsewhere in tryLoad/tryLDG; no .td change is needed.
general_case_safe: Non-atomic invariant global loads still take the LDG fast path: ISD::LOAD, NVPTXISD::MLoad, and the vector loads (LoadV2/V4/V8) all have getOpcode() != ISD::ATOMIC_LOAD, so canLowerToLDG still returns true and tryLDG still fires for them with their existing operand layout (LoadSDNode branch, or MLoad operands 3/4). The added clause only diverts ISD::ATOMIC_LOAD nodes, which are the sole AtomicSDNodes that can reach tryLoad/tryLoadVector (Select dispatches only LOAD/ATOMIC_LOAD/MLoad to tryLoad and the LoadV* opcodes to tryLoadVector; vector loads are never atomic). Those diverted atomic loads land on tryLoad's already-present, ordering-preserving ISD::ATOMIC_LOAD handling, so valid atomic loads now compile correctly instead of crashing, and no previously-LDG-eligible plain load changes behavior.

rationale: The pass's job is to rewrite register-form image instructions to symbol/index form *when the handle resolves to a compile-time symbol*. When it doesn't, the correct action is to keep the register form, not abort. This is already exactly what the LD_i64 CUDA case does (`return false`), and `processInstr` only swaps the opcode to index-form when `replaceImageHandle` returns true — so returning false from the default case leaves the register-form instruction (and its SELP/PHI/etc. def) intact. I confirmed empirically: a kernel whose tex handle comes from a function parameter (which hits the LD_i64 CUDA `return false` path) compiles to `tex.1d.v4.f32.s32 {%r2,%r3,%r4,%r5}, [%rd3, {%r1}];` — a valid register-form instruction with the runtime handle in %rd3. The select case is identical: the SELP_b64 result register feeds the register-form tex, giving correct runtime selection between the two handles. The recursive COPY/nvvm_move_i64 case also becomes correct: when it recurses into a SELP and gets false back, it returns false (keeps register form) and does not erase the COPY. Changing the default from llvm_unreachable to `return false` is the minimal fix; it is a .cpp change so no tablegen rebuild is needed.
general_case_safe: All existing symbol-rewriting paths are untouched: LD_i64 (non-CUDA), texsurf_handles (global), and nvvm_move_i64/COPY still rewrite to symbols exactly as before, and a non-select texsurf_handles use still folds to the `[tex0, {...}]` index form (verified). Only previously-unreachable defs change behavior: instead of aborting/UB they now keep the register form. On modern CUDA/sm_30+ targets register-form handle instructions are the normal, valid model (the param-handle control proves this), so all realistic runtime-handle uses now compile correctly. On the legacy image-handles-disabled (old Fermi/NVCL) path where register handles are unsupported, leaving register form is no worse than the prior llvm_unreachable abort/UB and never produces a silently-wrong result. The select's source handles (texsurf_handles mov.u64 of the globals) remain live and feed the SELP, preserving correct runtime semantics.

rationale: The over-align branch (max(16, ABIalign)) is justified only because the compiler controls all call sites of a local-linkage, non-address-taken function and byval params are caller-allocated copies in .param space. That justification fails for a kernel: its .param argument buffer is allocated and filled by the host/CUDA driver from natural ABI alignment, which the compiler does not control. Linkage (internal/private vs external) is irrelevant to that fact, so the gate must exclude kernels explicitly. The fix adds isKernelFunction(*F) to the early-return-ABI-align condition and removes the now-redundant assert (which was an unfounded invariant — the verifier accepts internal/private ptx_kernel). isKernelFunction is already available: NVVMProperties.h is included at line 16 of NVPTXUtilities.cpp and defines isKernelFunction(const Function&) inline. After the fix the repro compiles and emits `.param .align 4 .b8 ik_param_0[4]` (i32 ABI align = 4), matching what the host lays out, instead of crashing or emitting `.param .align 16`. All transitive callers (getFunctionByValParamAlign, getFunctionArgumentAlignment, NVPTXAsmPrinter IsKernelFunc path line 1414/1430, NVPTXISelLowering return-align line 4205, SetByValParamAlign line 67) route through this function with the kernel's F and now consistently get ABI alignment.
general_case_safe: The common case is unchanged. Non-kernel functions: kernels are identified solely by CallingConv::PTX_Kernel, so ordinary device functions never match isKernelFunction and still take the existing max(16, ABIalign) over-align path that enables 128-bit vectorized param loads. External/linkonce/weak functions and address-taken functions still early-return ABI align exactly as before (those conditions are evaluated unchanged). The F==nullptr call from NVPTXISelLowering.cpp:1262 still returns ABI align via the !F check. The only behavior that changes is for functions with CallingConv::PTX_Kernel AND local linkage AND not address-taken: previously assert-abort (debug) or wrong over-align (release); now correct ABI align. There is no valid configuration in which a kernel's host-filled byval/param slot should be over-aligned beyond ABI, so narrowing the over-align path to exclude kernels cannot regress a correct use. Removing the assert loses no checking because its predicate is provably violable by verifier-accepted IR; the new code handles that case correctly rather than asserting on it.

Safe for the general/common case. The unmodified-width case (no trunc between guard and shift, the dominant pattern from `n >= 32 ? 0 : x >> n` where n is the shift's own i32 type) keeps `ShiftAmt.getValueSizeInBits() == ClampAmtBits`, so the new condition is false and the combine fires exactly as before. The guard only adds a bail-out, never a wrong rewrite: it returns SDValue() (leaving the correct generic select+shift lowering in place) precisely when a wider guarded amount could be truncated lossily. Provably-narrowable amounts (zext-style, high bits known zero) still take the clamp path, so no regression in the cases the combine was written to optimize. The fix is a .cpp change (no tablegen), so no PTX-validity or arch-predicate concerns; it does not alter behavior for byte/i16/i32/i64 shifts whose guard matches the shift width.

rationale: Root cause is the per-element flattening of <N x i1> in the calling-convention decomposition: getPreferredVectorAction returns TypeSplitVector for i1 vectors, so the default getNumRegistersForCallingConv/getRegisterTypeForCallingConv report <N x i1> as N x i1, each lowered to a 1-byte param load/store at offsets 0..N-1. The slot, declared from getTypeAllocSize = ceil(N/8) bytes (packed, bit i -> byte i/8), is therefore overrun and the kernel ABI mismatches the host (which fills only the packed byte). The fix overrides the two calling-conv register hooks so that a fixed <N x i1> with N>=2 is reported as ONE packed integer register of ceil(N/8) bytes (i8/i16/i32/i64). Because the generic LowerArguments/LowerCall/LowerReturn build Ins/Outs from these same hooks, and ComputePTXValueVTs also calls them (on the whole, non-flattened vector, since ComputeValueVTs keeps vectors intact), both sides now agree on a single i8/iK entry at offset 0 whose store size equals the declared slot size. The generic getCopyToPartsVector/getCopyFromPartsVector NumParts==1 path then inserts the canonical BITCAST <N x i1> <-> iK (with a trunc/anyext to the byte for N not a multiple of 8), packing element i into bit i exactly as the global/x86 layout requires. For the repro, ComputePTXValueVTs now yields [i8]@0; LowerFormalArguments emits `ld.param.b8 [kern_param_0]`, the value is BITCAST i8 -> <8 x i1>, and extractelement 7 + zext lowers to (byte0 >> 7) & 1, returning 1 for host input 0x80 — matching the NOTES Expected and the x86 oracle (g8 = {129}). Verified the bit ordering against `store <8 x i1>` (shl/or pack into byte0) and globals g8/g4. I could not build, so I verified signatures against the base-class virtuals (TargetLoweringBase in TargetLowering.h: MVT getRegisterTypeForCallingConv(LLVMContext&, CallingConv::ID, EVT) const and unsigned getNumRegistersForCallingConv(LLVMContext&, CallingConv::ID, EVT) const) and confirmed divideCeil and MVT::INVALID_SIMPLE_VALUE_TYPE are available; the existing getNumRegisters override establishes the TargetLoweringBase:: qualifier style. Note: this also fixes the same latent bug for <2 x i1> fcmp returns, masked-store mask params (e.g. masked-store-variable-mask.ll), etc., so several NVPTX test CHECK lines will need regeneration with update_llc_test_checks.py; this is expected test churn, not a regression.
general_case_safe: Only fixed-length i1 vectors with N>=2 and a 1/2/4/8-byte packed footprint are intercepted (guarded by VT.isSimple(), VT.isVector(), !isScalableVector(), getVectorElementType()==MVT::i1, getVectorNumElements()>=2, and NumBytes in {1,2,4,8}). All byte-or-larger element types, scalars (including scalar i1, already handled as i8 elsewhere), <1 x i1>, scalable vectors, and odd packed widths (e.g. v9..v15i1, v128i1) fall through to the unchanged TargetLoweringBase implementation, so existing valid lowerings are unaffected. The chosen packed integer (i8/i16/i32/i64) has store size exactly equal to getTypeAllocSize(<N x i1>) = ceil(N/8) bytes, so the .param slot declared by the AsmPrinter (from getTypeAllocSize) and the single register access agree — no OOB, no slot/register size mismatch, and the host-visible kernel ABI (one packed byte/word) is honored. The two overrides stay mutually consistent (1 register of the packed type), and since NumParts==1 the generic part-copy code never consults getVectorTypeBreakdownForCallingConv, so no breakdown assertion can mismatch. Worst case for an unhandled exotic width is the pre-existing behavior, i.e. no new breakage.

rationale: Root cause is a design defect that cannot be fully fixed within the permitted edit target (NVPTX backend + IntrinsicsNVVM.td). Signedness is lost in clang BEFORE the backend: clang/lib/CodeGen/TargetBuiltins/NVPTX.cpp:616-643 lowers BOTH the signed builtins (__nvvm_atom_*_{max,min}_gen_i) AND the unsigned ones (_ui/_ul/_ull) to the IDENTICAL intrinsic int_nvvm_atomic_{max,min}_gen_i_{cta,sys}. At ISel there is no bit left to distinguish them, so any backend-only change can only pick ONE fixed lowering: keeping signed miscompiles unsigned (the current bug); switching to unsigned would instead miscompile signed atomicMax_block(int*) -- moving the bug rather than fixing it. A correct fix must (1) add signedness-carrying intrinsics (done here: int_nvvm_atomic_{umax,umin}_gen_i_{cta,sys}), (2) wire the currently-dead .u32/.u64 patterns to them (done here, via a new IntOpStr param that decouples the intrinsic op name from the PTX asm mnemonic so asm stays max.u32/min.u64), AND (3) reroute the unsigned builtins in clang to the new unsigned intrinsics. Step (3) is mandatory for correctness and is OUTSIDE the allowed edit scope; without it the new intrinsics are dead and unsigned builtins still emit the signed intrinsic, so the repro output is unchanged. Hence fixable=false. The edits above are the best-effort backend/td half of the real upstream fix; they are safe to land alone (they only add new, currently-unused selectable intrinsics and change no existing selection) but are incomplete without the companion clang change. Note: existing test llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/atomics-with-scope.ll asserts the signed forms for these intrinsics and would continue to pass, since the signed intrinsic still selects .s32/.s64.
general_case_safe: The td edits do not alter selection for any existing intrinsic: the new IntOpStr parameter defaults to OpStr, so every current ATOM2S_impl/ATOM2N_impl caller (add/bitwise/exch/incdec and the signed _s32/_s64 minmax variants) builds exactly the same intrinsic name and PTX asm as before. The only behavioral change is that the previously-dead _u32/_u64 minmax patterns now key off the new int_nvvm_atomic_{umax,umin}_gen_i_* intrinsics (asm still max.u32/min.u64), so they no longer collide with the signed patterns. The signed path (int_nvvm_atomic_{max,min}_gen_i_*) continues to select .s32/.s64 unchanged, and predicates (hasAtomScope, hasAtomMinMax64) are preserved. Byte/word semantics and all non-minmax atomics are untouched. However, full end-to-end correctness still requires rerouting the _ui/_ul/_ull builtins in clang, which is outside the permitted edit target; the backend edits alone leave the repro output unchanged because clang still emits the signed intrinsic.

rationale: Root cause is a mismatch between buffer layout (reserves AllocSize bytes per symbol) and printing (always emits ptrSize bytes per symbol). The fix records each symbol's actual byte width (AllocSize) at addSymbol time, then (1) routes any aggregate containing a sub-pointer-sized symbol to the per-byte printBytes/mask() path instead of printWords, and (2) makes printBytes emit only the symbol's recorded byte width of mask() bytes (low bytes), advancing pos by that width. For ptrtoint(@g to i32) on nvptx64 this emits the low 4 bytes of g (0xFF(g),0xFF00(g),0xFF0000(g),0xFF000000(g)) followed by the next field's bytes — exactly the truncation x86 produces (.long g / .long 0x12345678). The mask() byte operator already extracts byte i of the symbol address, so emitting only the low N bytes is the correct truncation without any '& mask' inside mask(). The word path (printWords) cannot represent a half-symbol/half-constant word, so forcing the byte path is necessary; that path requires PTX>=7.1 (hasMaskOperator). On PTX<7.1 (e.g. sm_70 default PTX 6.0) the existing report_fatal_error fires, which is correct: a truncated symbolic address has no valid PTX<7.1 encoding, so a clean diagnostic replaces the prior silent miscompile (matching how packed-aggr.ll already errors for unrepresentable pointer aggregates). I did not run a build per instructions; reasoning verified the printBytes sentinel (symbolPosInBuffer end-marker) is never indexed into SymbolSizes because the loop exits at pos==InitializerCount before the sentinel symbol branch.
general_case_safe: Full-pointer symbols (size == ptrSize) make allSymbolsFullPtrSize() true, so routing is identical to before: such aggregates still take printWords (aligned, word-multiple) or printBytes (packed/unaligned) exactly as today, and printBytes still emits ptrSize bytes since symSize == ptrSize. All three addSymbol call sites pass the already-computed AllocSize, which equals ptrSize for genuine pointers and only differs for the narrow-ptrtoint case. Existing tests (packed-aggr.ll, addrspacecast-gvar.ll) use only full pointers and are unaffected. The single behavior change is confined to aggregates containing a ptrtoint to an integer narrower than the pointer — the exact buggy case: on PTX>=7.1 it now emits correctly-truncated bytes; on PTX<7.1 it emits a clean fatal diagnostic instead of wrong bytes. Byte-or-larger full-pointer symbols still take the existing path unchanged.

rationale: The crash and the related empty-range miscompile both flow through addRangeAttr, so the single cleanest fix is there. The degenerate input is exactly Low == truncated-High: in this pass that only ever arises from a meaningless 0-valued dimension (a product-derived bound of 0 makes ntid/nctaid/nctarank call addRangeAttr(MinX=1, MaxX+1=1), and tid calls addRangeAttr(0,0)). I detect Low==High BEFORE constructing ConstantRange, returning early so the asserting ctor is never invoked. I add a second guard after intersecting with the intrinsic's declared range: reqntid=0 produces a non-degenerate [0,1) that intersects to the empty set, which would otherwise attach a poison range; isEmptySet() now skips it. In both skip cases the intrinsic keeps its declared range (e.g. [1,1025) for ntid.x) — strictly correct, never narrowing to a wrong/empty range. I verified the repro crash (maxntid=0), the sibling crash (maxclusterrank=0 on cluster_nctaid.x / cluster_nctarank), and the reqntid=0 empty-range miscompile all funnel through this function, so one edit fixes the whole class. The control case maxntid=64 (range(i32 1,65)) and every range in test/CodeGen/NVPTX/intr-range.ll have Low!=High and are non-empty, so all existing behavior is unchanged. Cannot build here, but reasoned through each path. Adding a regression function (e.g. test_maxntid_zero, test_reqntid_zero, test_maxclusterrank_zero) to llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/intr-range.ll and regenerating with update_test_checks.py --check-globals all is the appropriate test follow-up.
general_case_safe: The legitimate full-domain wrap the existing comment documents is High==2^BitWidth with a real lower bound Low, e.g. cluster_nctarank with maxclusterrank=UINT_MAX -> addRangeAttr(1, 2^32) -> LowAP=1, HighAP=0; since 1 != 0 it is NOT skipped and still yields the wrapped range [1,0). Every range produced by valid inputs (tid [0,MaxX), ntid [MinX,MaxX+1), the cluster variants) has Low strictly less than High after truncation whenever the dimension is >= 1, so the Low==High guard fires only for the impossible 0-dimension cases. The isEmptySet guard only removes ranges with no possible value, which are never useful attributes. Existing tests (intr-range.ll) all have Low != High and non-empty intersections, so their CHECK output is unchanged. Byte/normal block configs are unaffected; only meaningless 0-threads-per-block annotations stop crashing/miscompiling and instead fall back to the intrinsic's declared range.

rationale: The assert is over-strict: the non-array scalar path already correctly handles a scalar that legalizes into multiple PTX pieces. MakeDeclareScalarParam(ParamSymbol, TySize) declares a single .param whose size is promoteScalarArgumentSize(TySize*8) (72 bits -> .param .b128), and the storing loop in the else-branch (lines 1558+) uses VectorizePTXValueVTs(VTs, Offsets, ArgAlign) to store the two i64 pieces at offsets 0 and 8 (emitting st.param.v2.b64). This exactly mirrors how the callee definition is already compiled: I verified that `llc -mtriple=nvptx64 -mcpu=sm_70` on a standalone i72 add emits `.visible .func (.param .b128 func_retval0) add_i72(.param .b128 add_i72_param_0, .param .b128 add_i72_param_1)` with `ld.param.v2.b64 {%rd1,%rd2}`. So the only thing wrong is the assert. I removed the ArgOuts.size()==1 assert and generalized the type-validity assert (which previously only inspected ArgOuts[0]) to check every legalized piece via all_of, preserving its intent. all_of is already used unqualified in this file (STLExtras.h is included). The return-value path (lines 1632-1641, 1738+) had no analogous size==1 assert and already handled the i72 return, so no change is needed there.
general_case_safe: Single-piece scalars (i32, i64, f32, f64, pointers, i1->i8) still legalize to exactly one ArgOut, so they pass the generalized type check trivially and select the identical MakeDeclareScalarParam path with unchanged output. Scalars >= 128 bits, aggregates, vectors, half and bfloat still take the shouldPassAsArray array path (MakeDeclareArrayParam), unchanged. Byval args are unchanged. The only behavioral difference is that previously-aborting multi-piece scalar integers in [65,127] now compile, and the PTX they produce (single .param promoted to .b128 holding the two i64 pieces) matches the existing callee-side declaration and the prototype emitted by getPrototype, which both already use promoteScalarArgumentSize for the same widths — so caller and callee remain ABI-consistent.

rationale: The fix promotes only non-fundamental-width integer kernel scalar params to a valid PTX type, leaving all other cases byte-for-byte identical. The kernel non-pointer scalar branch now: (1) keeps the i1 -> u8 special case; (2) for an IntegerType whose width is NOT one of 8/16/32/64, computes promoteScalarArgumentSize(BitWidth) and emits `.u<Size>` for Size<=64 or `.b<Size>` for Size>64; (3) for everything else (fundamental-width ints i8/i16/i32/i64 and all non-integer scalars f32/f64/half/bfloat) falls through to the unchanged getPTXFundamentalTypeStr(Ty). promoteScalarArgumentSize is already used and in scope two lines below (NVPTXUtilities.h is included). For the repro k_i48: promoteScalarArgumentSize(48)=64 -> `.param .u64 k_i48_param_0`, exactly the NOTES Expected, and consistent with the body's `ld.param.b64`. This mirrors the proven-correct non-kernel path immediately below (which emits `.b<promoteScalarArgumentSize>`), and the formal-argument loads in LowerFormalArguments use ComputePTXValueVTs/VectorizePTXValueVTs offsets that are identical for kernel and non-kernel, so the promoted slot is always >= the load width and at offset 0. The `Size<=64 ? "u" : "b"` split avoids emitting an illegal `.u128`: i65..i127 (not diverted by shouldPassAsArray since <128 bits) currently crash on getPTXFundamentalTypeStr's llvm_unreachable, and now emit a valid `.b128` matching the non-kernel reference (`.param .b128` + ld.param.v2.b64). I verified the buggy output (.u48), the non-kernel reference output (.b32/.b64/.b128), the body load widths, and the i65 crash with the built llc before editing; I could not rebuild to confirm the patched output but the logic is mechanical.
general_case_safe: Fundamental-width integer kernel params (i8/i16/i32/i64) and all non-integer scalars are untouched: the new condition excludes widths 8/16/32/64, so those fall to the unchanged `else` branch and still emit `.u8`/`.u16`/`.u32`/`.u64` and `f32`/`f64`/`b16` exactly as before, preserving the existing kernel ABI and all golden tests (e.g. i1-param.ll's `.param .u8`, kernel i32 -> `.param .u32`). Only previously-invalid output is changed: non-fundamental widths that ptxas already rejected (.u48/.u24/.u17/.u3/.u40/.u56) now become valid promoted `.u32`/`.u64`, and the i65..i127 widths that previously crashed llc now emit valid `.b128`. The promoted size always >= the body's load width and the param is at offset 0, so the loader (which derives offsets independently of the declaration string) stays consistent. Pointers, byval, and aggregate/vector/>=128-bit scalar params take entirely separate earlier branches and are unaffected.

rationale:
Root cause: ATOM2N_impl builds the PTX op string as `op_str = OpStr # "." # TypeStr` (line 2657), and F_ATOMIC_2_INTRINSIC builds `asm_str = "atom" # sem_str # as_str # "." # op_str` (line 2486). PTX ISA grammar makes .noftz a MANDATORY part of atom.add for .f16/.f16x2/.bf16/.bf16x2; ptxas rejects the op without it.

Fix: change only the TypeStr argument for the f16/bf16 entries in ATOM2_add_impl to `"noftz.f16"`/`"noftz.bf16"`. This makes op_str become `add.noftz.f16`/`add.noftz.bf16` and the full asm string `atom.cta.add.noftz.f16` / `atom.sys.add.noftz.bf16`, exactly matching the non-scoped path (lines 2586-2587) and the NOTES' Expected output.

Why TypeStr is the right knob: TypeStr in this multiclass family is used in exactly one place — constructing op_str (the emitted PTX text). The intrinsic name lookup in ATOM2N_impl uses the separate IntTypeStr argument (`"f"`), not TypeStr (lines 2659-2661). The tablegen record-name suffix (`_f16`/`_bf16`) is hardcoded in ATOM2_add_impl's `defm` lines and is independent of TypeStr. So changing TypeStr only alters the PTX assembly string and nothing else (no intrinsic-matching, no record-name, no predicate change). grep confirms the only other TypeStr at line 6000 is in an unrelated multiclass.

Scope kept minimal: f32/f64 are untouched because those types legitimately have no .noftz qualifier; the integer variants are untouched.
general_case_safe: Only the two FP-half types that require .noftz (f16, bf16) are touched. f32/f64 and all integer atom.add variants keep their existing TypeStr and emit unchanged PTX. The intrinsic-to-instruction matching is driven by IntTypeStr/SpaceStr/scope (unchanged), and the tablegen record names (`_f16`/`_bf16`) are fixed in the defm lines (unchanged), so no patterns are renamed or remapped — valid uses still select the same intrinsics. The emitted string now exactly matches the already-correct non-scoped path's `add.noftz.f16`/`add.noftz.bf16`, so the scoped path produces well-formed PTX with the same denormals-preserved semantics the intrinsic intends.

rationale:

rationale: The root cause is that isInvariantLoad() never inspects the load's volatility before stamping !invariant.load. The minimal fix adds an early `if (I->isVolatile()) return false;` in isInvariantLoad, using the const Instruction *I that is already passed in. Instruction::isVolatile() (lib/IR/Instruction.cpp:1203) dispatches to LoadInst::isVolatile() for the load case, so a `load volatile` is correctly excluded and falls through to the normal lowering path, which emits `ld.volatile.global.b32` — exactly the output produced when the `readonly` attribute is absent (the NOTES' stated Expected). I placed the check immediately after the global-AS check and before the existing-metadata and getUnderlyingObjects work, which is the natural spot and avoids unnecessary analysis for volatile loads. The fix touches only the IR-tagging pass; ISel's canLowerToLDG is left unchanged because, once the bogus invariant tag is gone, the load is no longer N.isInvariant() and tryLDG is never reached for it.
general_case_safe: Non-volatile invariant-eligible loads are completely unaffected: the new check only short-circuits when I->isVolatile() is true, so ordinary loads from constant globals or noalias-readonly/grid-constant kernel args still get tagged exactly as before (verified: the existing all_of(Objs,...) predicate is unchanged). The masked_load intrinsic path also passes I (the IntrinsicInst) here; Instruction::isVolatile() returns false for masked.load (it has no volatile flag), so masked-load tagging behavior is preserved. The change only ever removes incorrect invariant tagging from a load whose LLVM IR explicitly marks it volatile — which can never be a legitimate invariant load — so it cannot introduce any new miscompile and strictly fixes the dropped-volatile case.

rationale: The root cause is at NVPTXISelLowering.cpp:7543-7544: `if (Ty->isFloatTy()) return AtomicExpansionKind::None;` selects the native PTX `atom.add.f32` for every f32 atomicrmw fadd. The fix gates that `None` return on the function's f32 denormal mode being `PreserveSign` (FTZ), mirroring the existing `useF32FTZ()` helper at lines 146-148 (`MF.getDenormalMode(APFloat::IEEEsingle()).Output == DenormalMode::PreserveSign`). I used `AI->getFunction()->getDenormalMode(...)` because shouldExpandAtomicRMWInIR only has the IR AtomicRMWInst (no MachineFunction yet); `Instruction::getFunction()` (Instruction.h:221) and `Function::getDenormalMode(const fltSemantics&)` (Function.h:720) provide the same query. Both `APFloat::IEEEsingle()` and `DenormalMode::PreserveSign` are already used and in scope in this file. When the mode is IEEE (the default for the repro, which has no denormal-fp-math attribute), the f32 branch no longer returns None and control falls through to `return AtomicExpansionKind::CmpXChg;` at line 7548, which AtomicExpandPass lowers to a non-flushing CAS loop using a real fadd — matching the x86 oracle (addss + lock cmpxchgl) and NVPTX's own plain `fadd float` (add.rn.f32). rationale:
Root cause: the `// Formatted` loop in IntrinsicsNVVM.td (lines 2360-2364) generates int_nvvm_sust_p_* intrinsics for the full vec list including sub-word types (TV_I8, TV_I16, TV_V2I8, TV_V2I16, TV_V4I8, TV_V4I16). NVPTXIntrinsics.td then defines matching SUST_P_* instructions whose mnemonics are `sust.p.*.b8`/`.b16`, which the DAG patterns select. PTX (sect 9.7.12.2) defines the formatted store only with .b32, so these emit invalid PTX that ptxas rejects.

Fix: (1) Restrict the formatted-store intrinsic generation to the i32 vec types [TV_I32, TV_V2I32, TV_V4I32], the only data type PTX's sust.p accepts. (2) Remove the now-orphaned subword `defm SUST_P_*` lines in NVPTXIntrinsics.td. These must be removed because each subword multiclass does `!cast<Intrinsic>("int_nvvm_" # !tolower(NAME))`; once the subword intrinsics are gone, those casts would fail at tablegen time. I left every `.b32` defm (including the array `.b32` forms) intact so all currently-valid uses still select normally.

Scope note: I deliberately kept the `.b32` array forms (SUST_P_*_ARRAY_I32/V2I32/V4I32) even though surf-tex.py also flags formatted-array stores as PTX-unsupported — that is a separate issue beyond this repro, and those forms are not part of the reported bug. Removing only the subword forms is the minimal change that fixes the repro.

Effect: llvm.nvvm.sust.p.1d.i8.trap / .2d.i16.trap (and v2/v4 subword forms) become unknown intrinsics, producing a clean front-end/IR error instead of bogus PTX. The valid `.b32` formatted stores are unchanged.

Verification done: confirmed the repro currently emits `sust.p.1d.b8.trap` and `sust.p.2d.b16.trap`. Confirmed no codegen .ll test exercises any sust.p subword form (surf-write.ll/surf-write-cuda.ll contain no sust.p), and these mnemonics appear only in surf-tex.py's "known/untested" exception list with the comment "FIXME: spec does not list any sust.p variants other than b32". Confirmed no clang builtin/header/test references the sust_p subword intrinsics, so removing them needs no clang-side change. Note: surf-tex.py's generated `instructions` self-check exception list will need the subword sust.p entries removed when that test is next regenerated, but that is a test-generator update, not part of the source fix; the .ll tests themselves don't reference these.
general_case_safe: The general/common case is the valid formatted-surface store with a 32-bit channel (`sust.p.*.b32`), which is the only data type PTX defines for sust.p. All `.b32` intrinsics and their selection patterns (TV_I32/TV_V2I32/TV_V4I32, for 1d/2d/3d and the array forms) are preserved verbatim, so every currently-valid use still selects to the same correct instruction. The only behavior change is for the sub-word formatted-store intrinsics, which today can ONLY produce invalid PTX (sust.p.*.b8/.b16 — rejected by ptxas); there is no valid program that relies on them. After the fix those calls become unknown intrinsics → a clean IR-level error rather than silent bad PTX, which is the desired outcome. The unformatted store (sust.b) keeps its full .b8/.b16/.b32/.b64 set untouched.

rationale: The atom selection path takes its addsp operand from getAddrSpace(N), which returns the raw memory address space (Const/Local/EntryParam/DeviceParam all returned), and the InstPrinter prints those as .const/.param/.local for atom. But PTX 'atom' supports only .global/.shared/generic. I verified empirically (ld.const.b32 [%rd1] for a const-space load, and atom.global / atom (generic) for global/generic atomics) that for const/param the register holds a WINDOW-RELATIVE address, not a generic address. So silently dropping the qualifier to use generic addressing would atomically access the wrong location -- a miscompile -- and modifying const/param memory is UB anyway. The correct, non-silencing behavior is a clean compile-time diagnostic, matching NVPTX's existing report_fatal_error pattern for other unlowererable atomic configurations (seq_cst RMW, acq_rel RMW). I added a static helper getAtomicAddrSpace that returns the address space for the atom-valid spaces and report_fatal_errors for Const/Local/EntryParam/DeviceParam, then routed the atom GetAddSp SDNodeXForm (which feeds every F_ATOMIC_2/F_ATOMIC_3 form) and the 128-bit selectAtomicSwap128 path through it. getAtomicAddrSpace is declared static in the header next to getAddrSpace; the XForm body runs as a method of the generated selector and calls it the same way it called getAddrSpace. NVPTXUtilities.h (addressSpaceToString) and FormatVariadic.h are already included in the .cpp and 'using namespace llvm' is in effect.
general_case_safe: The shared getAddrSpace is left completely unchanged, so the load/store paths (lines 588, 1153, 1231, 1427, 1474) continue to emit valid ld.const / st.local / ld.param etc. -- those qualifiers are legal for ld/st. Only the atom-specific consumers (the GetAddSp XForm used by all F_ATOMIC_2/F_ATOMIC_3 patterns, and selectAtomicSwap128) now go through getAtomicAddrSpace. For the common/valid atom cases -- Generic, Global, Shared, and SharedCluster -- getAtomicAddrSpace returns the address space unchanged, so atom.add.u32 / atom.global.add.u32 / atom.shared.add.u32 / atom.shared::cluster... still select and print exactly as before (verified Global -> atom.global.add.u32 and Generic -> atom.add.u32 in the current build). Only the four spaces PTX atom genuinely cannot encode (Const/Local/EntryParam/DeviceParam) now produce a clear compiler error instead of unassemblable PTX, which is the design-preferred outcome for an inherently-invalid (UB, read-only/parameter memory) atomic.

rationale: The NVPTX variable for a half/bfloat global is declared as `.b16` (getPTXFundamentalTypeStr returns "b16" for Half/BFloat: "fp16 and bf16 are stored as .b16 for compatibility with pre-sm_53 PTX assembly"). A `.b16` slot is a bit/integer type, so its initializer must be a raw 16-bit integer, exactly how integer globals are printed (`O << CI->getValue()` -> `.u16 i = 15360;`). The fix emits `APF.bitcastToAPInt().getZExtValue()` for Half/BFloat, producing the raw bits: 0xH3C00 -> 15360 (0x3C00, half 1.0) and 0xR3F80 -> 16256 (0x3F80, bfloat 1.0). This matches the x86 oracle, which stores raw bytes `0x3c00` and `0x3f80` (`.short 0x3c00 # half 1`, `.short 0x3f80 # bfloat 1`), and matches the existing bufferLEByte array-element path, which already bitcasts Half/BFloat to their integer representation. I added the case as an early return before the Float/Double chain so the existing float/double formatting (`0f`/`0d` hex literals) is untouched. The fp16/bf16 zero-init scalar case already worked (printed `.b16 name;` with no initializer because null values skip printScalarConstant); this only adds the previously-crashing non-zero path.
general_case_safe: Float (FloatTyID) and double (DoubleTyID) globals still take the exact existing `0f`/`0d` hex-literal path — the new branch returns early only for Half/BFloat, which previously hit llvm_unreachable, so there is no behavior change for any type that compiled before. fp128 and larger types never reach printFPConstant (they take the aggregate/byte-buffer branch in printModuleLevelGV). The emitted integer value is type-consistent with the `.b16` declaration the same function/file already produces for half/bfloat, so valid PTX is generated, and the value bit-for-bit matches the x86 oracle and the existing array-element lowering. The other caller (MI operand printer at the printFPConstant call for MO.getFPImm) is unaffected for float/double and would previously have crashed for half/bfloat too, so no regression.

getAddrSpace() static_casts the IR address space to NVPTX::AddressSpace and switches over the named enumerators (Generic=0, Global=1, Shared=3, Const=4, Local=5, SharedCluster=7, EntryParam=101, DeviceParam). The fix replaces that abort with `return NVPTX::AddressSpace::Generic`. In NVPTXInstPrinter (line 353), Generic prints no state-space qualifier, i.e. a plain `ld`/`st`, which is exactly the correct conservative lowering for a pointer in an address space the backend has no special segment for. The x86 oracle confirms this: `llc -mtriple=x86_64` lowers `load i32, ptr addrspace(2)`/`addrspace(6)` to ordinary `mov` loads/stores (generic semantics, no special segment). This single change covers every caller (tryLoad/tryLoadVector/tryStore/tryStoreVector/the atomic path at 2280/getOperationOrderings at 564) because they all obtain CodeAddrSpace through this one helper.

rationale: The input IR is well-formed (verifier-accepted), but NVPTX/PTX has no scalable vectors at all, so a scalable-vector byval kernel parameter genuinely cannot be lowered. The pre-existing failure is an *internal* fatal error (reportFatalInternalError) with a crash trace and a 'please report an LLVM bug' banner -- the wrong diagnostic for valid-but-unsupported input. The fix converts it to `reportFatalUsageError`, which ErrorHandling.h documents as exactly for 'known unsupported/unimplemented functionality' and 'invalid inputs': it exits cleanly with code 1, no crash trace, no bug-report request. `reportFatalUsageError` is already in scope via the existing `#include \"llvm/Support/ErrorHandling.h\"` and `using namespace llvm;`. The guard uses `Type::isScalableTy()`, which is precisely the set of types whose getAllocationSize returns a scalable TypeSize (scalable vectors and aggregates containing them). I placed it before CreateAlloca/replaceAllUsesWith so no half-lowered IR is produced; since the function is [[noreturn]], it also prevents the secondary DAG-selection crash the NOTES mention on the read-only path -- this single early check covers every entry point into copyByValParam. I considered DiagnosticInfoUnsupported (the per-function diagnostic used elsewhere in NVPTX), but it does not halt the pipeline immediately (it relies on llc checking HasErrors only after the full codegen run), so it would risk a secondary ISel crash on the un-lowered scalable byval before that check fires; reportFatalUsageError guarantees a single clean exit.

Every fixed-width byval type (structs, fixed-width vectors, scalars -- the entire common case) has isScalableTy()==false and takes the existing, unchanged alloca+memcpy path. No valid lowering is foreclosed because PTX has no scalable vectors, so the only behavioral change is replacing an internal-error abort with a clean usage error; legitimate non-scalable byval kernel params are completely unaffected. Placing the check before any IR mutation (CreateAlloca/RAUW) and using a [[noreturn]] reporter means no inconsistent IR state is ever produced.
