rationale: The fp8 m16n8k16/m16n8k32 MMA datapaths both require PTX 8.7 per the PTX ISA 8.7 release notes and per the in-tree generator llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/wmma.py is_mma_variant_supported, which rejects op.a.geom in [\"m16n8k16\",\"m16n8k32\"] with e4m3/e5m2 when ptx_version < 87. The existing .td clause only covered m16n8k16, so m16n8k32 fp8 fell through to the generic [hasSM<89>, hasPTX<84>] fp8 floor. Extending the 8.7 clause to also match m16n8k32 makes the predicate agree with the generator, so the repro (mma.sync.m16n8k32 ... f32.e4m3.e4m3.f32 at -mattr=+ptx84) now cannot-select (clean) instead of emitting invalid PTX under .version 8.4, exactly mirroring the already-correct m16n8k16 sibling behavior at ptx84.
general_case_safe: The generic [hasSM<89>, hasPTX<84>] fp8 clause is left intact, so non-MMA fp8 fragment intrinsics (WMMA load/store fragments, whose true type-floor is PTX 8.4 per is_type_supported) still select at PTX 8.4. Only the e4m3/e5m2 MMA datapaths at geom m16n8k16 OR m16n8k32 now require PTX 8.7, which is their real minimum arch — valid uses at sm_89/ptx87+ still select correctly, and the only behavior change is that m16n8k32 fp8 MMA at ptx84-86 now gives a clean Cannot-select rather than ptxas-invalid PTX. The sparse MMA_SP/block_scale paths are unaffected (they already pull a higher guard via the f32 accumulator frag), and no other geom/type combination matches this clause.

rationale: The shared::cluster qualifier is selected as the AtomicCode:$addsp immediate in C++ (getAddrSpace) and printed verbatim by the generic LD<>/ST<> instruction classes, which carry no Requires<> predicate, so a tablegen guard cannot be attached without splitting the instruction per address space. The design rules explicitly endorse adding an explicit subtarget check in the C++ getMachineNode path that bypasses a tablegen Requires<>. I added a static helper checkAddrSpaceIsSupported that mirrors the file's existing report_fatal_error guards (the 32-bit shared-cluster check in SelectAddrSpaceCast, the Const check in tryStoreVector, the atom address-space check in getAtomicAddrSpace) and call it at the four ld/st emission chokepoints (tryLoad, tryLoadVector, tryStore, tryStoreVector) immediately after getAddrSpace and before any machine node or tryLDG fallback is created. The predicate Subtarget->hasClusters() is exactly the sm_90 && PTX78 floor the .shared::cluster qualifier requires, so the check fires precisely on invalid targets. The masked-load NVPTXISD::MLoad case is handled inside tryLoad and is therefore covered; tryLDG is only reached after the check and only applies to the global address space, never shared-cluster. I left the atomic path (getAtomicAddrSpace, which is static and reached from tablegen) untouched because it is not exercised by the repro and a clean fix there would require threading the subtarget through a static method; keeping the change minimal and scoped to the demonstrated + directly-parallel vector paths.
general_case_safe: On sm_90+ with PTX 7.8+ (Subtarget->hasClusters() == true) the helper is a no-op, so all legitimate shared::cluster loads/stores still select and emit exactly as before. All other address spaces (Generic/Global/Shared/Const/Local/Param) never equal NVPTX::AddressSpace::SharedCluster, so they are completely unaffected on every target. The only behavior change is that a shared::cluster load/store on a sub-sm_90 target now produces a clean fatal diagnostic instead of unassemblable PTX (ld.shared::cluster under .target sm_50), matching how the backend already rejects 32-bit shared::cluster casts and atom on unsupported spaces. The predicate matches the instruction's real minimum architecture (PTX ISA 7.8 / sm_90, per the release notes and the sibling cvta.shared::cluster [hasClusters] guard), so valid uses still select and only genuinely-invalid ones are rejected.

rationale: SelectAddrSpaceCast lowers shared::cluster casts by calling CurDAG->getMachineNode(NVPTX::cvta_shared_cluster_64/cvta_to_shared_cluster_64, ...). Instruction predicates like Requires<[hasClusters]> are only enforced during tablegen pattern-matched selection, not for nodes created directly via getMachineNode, so the [hasClusters] guard on these two defs is silently bypassed. The minimal fix mirrors the predicate in C++: hasClusters() is exactly SmVersion>=90 && PTXVersion>=78 (NVPTXSubtarget.h:107), the same condition the .td predicate encodes. I add the check right next to the existing 64-bit-mode report_fatal_error guard in both the NG_TO_G (cvta_shared_cluster_64) and G_TO_NG (cvta_to_shared_cluster_64) branches, matching surrounding style. Subtarget is already a member of this ISel class and is used for analogous capability checks elsewhere in the file (e.g. line 565 resolveScope uses hasClusters, line 304/542/571 use other Subtarget capability helpers). This turns invalid PTX into a clean compile-time diagnostic on unsupported targets. No .td is edited, so no tablegen rebuild is needed.
general_case_safe: On sm_90+/PTX7.8+ targets hasClusters() is true, so valid shared::cluster addrspacecasts still select cvta.shared::cluster / cvta.to.shared::cluster exactly as before — no change to the common case. The shared::cluster address space (addrspace 7) is only meaningful on cluster-capable hardware, so rejecting it below sm_90 cannot regress any valid program; it merely converts previously-emitted invalid PTX into a clear fatal error. The check is placed only in the two SHARED_CLUSTER switch cases, leaving all other address-space casts (global/shared/const/local/param) untouched. The guard predicate is the literal definition of hasClusters(), identical to the .td Requires<[hasClusters]> it backstops, so the C++ path and the tablegen path now agree.

edits.old_string: bool hasAtomSwap128() const { return SmVersion >= 90 && PTXVersion >= 83; }

rationale: The .sys scope is the *default* scope of the PTX atom instruction, so an ordinary (un-syncscope'd) i128 atomicrmw/cmpxchg resolves to NVPTX::Scope::System and prints the explicit `.sys` qualifier. That explicit qualifier on a .b128 atom is only legal from PTX ISA 8.4 onward, but hasAtomSwap128() enables b128 atomics from PTX 8.3, leaving a window where valid IR produces invalid PTX. The fix targets exactly that window: a new subtarget predicate hasAtomSwap128SysScope() (SmVersion>=90 && PTXVersion>=84) gates whether the explicit `.sys` form may be emitted. In selectAtomicSwap128 (the C++ getMachineNode path that bypasses the instruction's tablegen Requires<>), when the resolved scope is System and that predicate is false, the scope operand is set to NVPTX::Scope::DefaultDevice, which the InstPrinter maps to *no* scope qualifier (printAtomicCode, NVPTXInstPrinter.cpp:332-333). The emitted PTX becomes `atom.relaxed.exch.b128` / `atom.relaxed.cas.b128`, which falls back to the instruction's implicit default scope — .sys — so system-scope semantics are preserved exactly while the text is legal at PTX 8.3. I chose to fix the C++ selection rather than bump hasAtomSwap128() to ptx84, because bumping the gate would wrongly disable *all* b128 atomics at PTX 8.3, including the .cta/.gpu/.cluster forms that ARE legal there (per the NOTES). DefaultDevice (rather than Thread) is used because its enum comment documents "PTX op implicit/default scope," matching the intent; both print empty, so the resulting PTX is identical.
general_case_safe: Only the System-scope-at-PTX<8.4 case is rewritten. Explicit narrower syncscopes (Block/.cta, Device/.gpu, Cluster/.cluster) are untouched and remain valid at PTX 8.3, so valid 8.3 b128 atomics with those scopes still select and print correctly. At PTX>=8.4 hasAtomSwap128SysScope() is true, so the explicit `.sys` form is emitted exactly as before — the existing atomics-b128.ll test (which runs at ptx84 and expects `atom.relaxed.sys...b128`) is unchanged. The hasAtomSwap128() legality gate is left alone, so the set of targets on which b128 atomics select at all is unchanged. The rewrite only ever maps System -> DefaultDevice, and per the PTX ISA the atom instruction's implicit default scope is .sys, so the system-scope memory semantics are preserved exactly (no scope narrowing, no miscompile). 64-bit-and-smaller atomics never reach selectAtomicSwap128 and are completely unaffected.

rationale:
Root cause: NVPTXAtomicLower.cpp (run at NVPTXTargetMachine.cpp:308, before ISel) is the dedicated pass that strips local-memory atomics to load/store, but it only collected AtomicRMWInst. cmpxchg on addrspace(5) was therefore never lowered and reached the F_ATOMIC_3 cas patterns (b16/b32/b64) and selectAtomicSwap128/ATOM_CAS_B128 (b128), all of which print the .local state space via the addsp operand -> invalid PTX.

Fix: also collect AtomicCmpXchgInst whose pointer is in ADDRESS_SPACE_LOCAL and lower them with the existing llvm::lowerAtomicCmpXchgInst helper (already declared in Transforms/Utils/LowerAtomic.h, which is already #included; AtomicCmpXchgInst comes from IR/Instructions.h, also already included). That helper emits exactly load / icmp eq / select / store and packs the {value, i1} result via insertvalue -- the same load-compare-conditional-store semantics x86 emits (lock cmpxchgl ...) for these functions, which is correct because thread-private local memory cannot race, so dropping the atomicity/ordering is sound (this is the same rationale already used for the RMW case in this very pass, and mirrors AMDGPU returning AtomicExpansionKind::NotAtomic for PRIVATE_ADDRESS atomics in SIISelLowering.cpp). I separated the two work-lists/loops rather than templating, matching the file's plain style. No .td change, so no tablegen rebuild. Two iteration vectors are used so erasing instructions during lowering does not invalidate the instruction iteration.

Why not fix getAtomicAddrSpace / shouldExpandAtomicRMWInIR / add shouldExpandAtomicCmpXchgInIR(NotAtomic): those are downstream of this pass and would be redundant; doing the NotAtomic expansion in AtomicExpandPass also risks spurious fences because processAtomicInstr brackets RMW/CAS with fences (via shouldInsertFencesForAtomic) before the NotAtomic strip. Lowering here, before all of that, is the minimal single-site fix and is exactly what the pass was written to do.
general_case_safe: Only instructions whose pointer address space is exactly ADDRESS_SPACE_LOCAL (5) are touched; the new branch is an `else if` on AtomicCmpXchgInst, so non-local cmpxchg, all loads/stores, and every other instruction are untouched and continue to the normal ISel path (global/shared/generic cmpxchg still selects atom.cas as before). The atomicrmw handling is byte-for-byte unchanged (same dyn_cast, same AS check, same lowerAtomicRMWInst call), just renamed and moved into the shared loop. All cmpxchg widths are handled uniformly because lowerAtomicCmpXchgInst is type-agnostic, including the b128 path that previously went through selectAtomicSwap128. The lowering reproduces the architecturally correct single-thread semantics (matching x86's load/compare/store), not a silenced wrong result.

rationale: The fix mirrors the existing, correct guard in the sibling vector path tryStoreVector() (lines 1474-1478 of the same file), which does exactly `if (CodeAddrSpace == NVPTX::AddressSpace::Const) report_fatal_error("Cannot store to pointer that points to constant memory space");`. Storing to NVPTX::AddressSpace::Const is fundamentally invalid PTX — constant memory is read-only and the `st` instruction has no `.const` state space form. Inserting the identical guard right after CodeAddrSpace is computed in tryStore() makes the scalar path behave like the vector path: a store to const memory produces a clean diagnostic instead of silently-invalid `st.const` PTX that ptxas would reject. I matched on the `// Address Space Setting` comment + getAddrSpace line + following blank line + `SDLoc DL(ST);`, which is unique to tryStore() (in tryStoreVector the guard already sits between getAddrSpace and SDLoc, so that block does not match). No tablegen change is needed, so needs_td_rebuild=false. report_fatal_error is already used in this file and in tryStoreVector, so no new include is required.
general_case_safe: The guard only triggers when CodeAddrSpace == NVPTX::AddressSpace::Const (LLVM addrspace 4), which is never a valid store target in PTX — there is no legitimate scalar store to constant memory that this could break. All writable address spaces (Generic, Global, Shared, Local, Param) compare unequal and fall through to the unchanged existing selection path, so every valid scalar store still selects exactly as before. This is the same predicate the vector store path already uses, so the two paths now agree: store-to-const is rejected uniformly with a diagnostic rather than one path emitting bad PTX. Loads from constant memory are handled by a separate path (tryLoad) and are unaffected.

rationale: Three coordinated edits in NVPTXAsmPrinter.cpp make a nested BlockAddress flow through the same symbol-emission machinery used for GlobalValue/ConstantExpr pointer elements: (1) bufferLEByte's PointerTyID case now records the BlockAddress as a symbol via addSymbol (instead of falling through to a pure addZeros, which produced numSymbols()==0 and the all-zero .b8 output); (2) AggBuffer::printSymbol now accepts a BlockAddress in v0 and lowers it through lowerConstantForGV (the prior dyn_cast<ConstantExpr> branch hit llvm_unreachable for a BlockAddress); (3) lowerConstantForGV gains a BlockAddress case returning MCSymbolRefExpr::create(GetBlockAddressSymbol(BA), Ctx) — exactly what the base AsmPrinter::lowerBlockAddressConstant does. After the fix, the aligned full-pointer array case takes printWords (.u64 ba_arr[1] = {$L__tmp0}) and the unaligned packed-struct case takes the mask() printBytes path, both emitting the block-address label rather than zeros, matching the x86 oracle's `.quad .Ltmp0`. GetBlockAddressSymbol is a public AsmPrinter member and Constants.h (declaring BlockAddress) is already included, so no new includes are needed. Suggested regression test home: append array and packed-struct blockaddress globals to /Users/justinlebar/code/llvm2/llvm/test/CodeGen/NVPTX/globals_init.ll (hand-written CHECK-DAG file).
general_case_safe: Existing pointer element kinds are untouched: GlobalValue and ConstantExpr operands still take their original branches in bufferLEByte; only a true BlockAddress, which was previously dropped to zeros, now records a symbol. In printSymbol, isa<ConstantExpr>(v0) yields identical behavior to the old dyn_cast<ConstantExpr> for every prior input (cast<Constant>(v0) is the same ConstantExpr); BlockAddress is the only newly-accepted kind, replacing an llvm_unreachable. In lowerConstantForGV the new BlockAddress case is inserted before the ConstantExpr cast and the final 'Unknown constant value to lower!' unreachable, so all existing constants reach their existing handlers unchanged; a BlockAddress that previously crashed now lowers correctly. The change is purely additive for a previously-mishandled constant kind and does not alter byte-or-larger non-blockaddress aggregate layout.

rationale: printScalarConstant was the only remaining gap. The companion routines already support BlockAddress: lowerConstantForGV lowers `BlockAddress` via `MCSymbolRefExpr::create(GetBlockAddressSymbol(BA), Ctx)` (NVPTXAsmPrinter.cpp:1967-1968), AggBuffer::printSymbol already routes `isa<BlockAddress>(v0)` through lowerConstantForGV (line 1150-1151), and bufferLEByte's PointerTyID case already has an `isa<BlockAddress>(CPV)` addSymbol branch (line 1765-1766). So the minimal fix is to make printScalarConstant route a BlockAddress (and a ptrtoint(blockaddress) ConstantExpr, which it already handled) into the existing lowerConstantForGV path. I broadened the existing ConstantExpr branch to `isa<ConstantExpr, BlockAddress>` and pass CPV directly (dropping the now-unnecessary cast<Constant>, since CPV is already const Constant*). This mirrors the generic AsmPrinter::lowerConstant ordering (GlobalValue, then BlockAddress). Result: NVPTX emits a reference to the block-address label instead of crashing, matching x86's `.quad .Ltmp0`. Variadic isa<> and printMCExpr are already used in this file (e.g. isa<ConstantInt, ConstantFP> at line 1815), so the edit matches surrounding style. No regression test added per task scope; the natural home would be test/CodeGen/NVPTX/globals_init.ll.
general_case_safe: All previously handled scalar initializers are unchanged: ConstantInt, ConstantFP, ConstantPointerNull, and GlobalValue each return before reaching the modified branch. The modified branch still handles every ConstantExpr exactly as before (lowerConstantForGV(CPV, false) with CPV == the ConstantExpr), only additionally accepting BlockAddress, which lowerConstantForGV already lowers correctly. Any Constant kind that is neither of the handled types still hits the unchanged llvm_unreachable, preserving the existing diagnostic for genuinely unsupported constants. The dropped cast<Constant>(Cexpr) is a no-op since CPV is already const Constant*.

edits.old_string: unsigned getBufferSize() const { return Size; }

rationale: The aggregate case wrote bufferAggregateConstant's bytes (an aggregate's STORE size) but only padded when the caller's Bytes exceeded AllocSize. A non-pow2 vector writes fewer bytes than its alloc size, so the slot was left short. Instead of guessing the written count, I capture the real number of bytes emitted via curpos before/after bufferAggregateConstant, then zero-fill up to the slot the constant must occupy: max(Bytes, AllocSize) — Bytes when a struct field supplies the alloc-offset delta, AllocSize when an array element passes Bytes=0. This is fully recursive, so nested structs and arrays-of-vectors (where inter-element padding was also dropped) are fixed by the same code as each element re-enters bufferLEByte. I added a tiny getCurpos() accessor (curpos was private) mirroring the existing getBufferSize(). Verified the four NOTES cases (struct field, [2 x <3 x i32>], <3 x i16> struct, packed <{<3 x i32>,i32}>) and {<6 x i8>,i8} against the x86 oracle: the fix reproduces x86's offsets exactly (e.g. trailing i32 at byte 16, g sized 32 with 254 at offset 16).
general_case_safe: Byte-or-larger power-of-2 vectors are unaffected: their store size equals their alloc size, so Written == AllocSize and SlotSize - Written == 0 (no extra zeros). Structs/arrays of non-vector types already write their full alloc size (the struct branch telescopes element offsets), so Written == AllocSize and the new padding is 0 — identical to before. The only behavioral change is when bufferAggregateConstant wrote fewer than max(Bytes,AllocSize) bytes, which is exactly the buggy non-pow2-vector case. The old `Bytes > AllocSize` path is subsumed: for a struct field Written==AllocSize so SlotSize-Written == Bytes-AllocSize when Bytes>AllocSize. Top-level vector globals are untouched because printModuleLevelGV calls bufferAggregateConstant directly (sized to the vector's store size), not bufferLEByte, so a standalone <3 x i32> still emits [12]. No buffer overflow: the top-level AggBuffer is sized to the top type's alloc size, and per-field/per-element SlotSizes telescope exactly to that size, so curpos never exceeds Size.

rationale: The crash is the implicit scalable-TypeSize-to-unsigned conversion inside the size comparison at line 75. The minimal fix computes the TypeSize once and (a) explicitly skips scalable types via isScalable(), and (b) uses getFixedValue() for the threshold compare instead of the implicit operator ScalarTy(). Skipping scalable loads keeps them out of AggrLoads, so the second identical crash site at line 108 (unsigned NumLoads = DL.getTypeStoreSize(...)) is also never reached for scalable types and needs no change. A scalable load/store left untouched falls through to the normal NVPTX instruction-selection path, which is the correct behavior — this transform exists only to turn LARGE FIXED-SIZE aggregate copies into loops, and a scalable copy fundamentally cannot be expressed as a fixed-size copy loop (the ConstantInt CopyLen built from NumLoads requires a compile-time byte count). No x86 oracle was needed: this is a crash bug, and the x86 path crashes on the same IR for an unrelated reason (combineStore), so it offers no layout to match; the correct fix is simply to stop NVPTXLowerAggrCopies from aborting on valid IR.
general_case_safe: For every fixed-width aggregate type (arrays, structs, fixed-width vectors) getFixedValue() returns exactly the same uint64_t that the old implicit TypeSize->ScalarTy conversion returned, so the existing threshold semantics are byte-for-byte unchanged: sizes < 128 still `continue` (skip), sizes >= 128 still get added to AggrLoads and lowered to a memmove/copy loop. The only new behavior is that scalable vectors hit the added isScalable() `continue` and are left for normal isel rather than crashing the pass. This cannot regress the common large-fixed-aggregate-copy lowering, and it cannot silently produce a wrong result — scalable loads are simply not transformed, so downstream isel decides whether to select them or emit a clean target-capability diagnostic.

edits.old_string:
#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineFunctionPass.h"
#include "llvm/CodeGen/MachineRegisterInfo.h"

assert(TexHandleDef.getOperand(7).isSymbol() && "Load is not a symbol!");
    StringRef Sym = TexHandleDef.getOperand(7).getSymbolName();

rationale: The LD_i64 branch unconditionally assumed the handle's defining load reads a kernel-parameter symbol (operand 7 == ExternalSymbol). When the handle instead comes from a generic load whose base is a register/frameindex, operand 7 is not a symbol; the assert fires in debug and getSymbolName() reads a bogus union field in release. The NVPTX image-handle model has no way to synthesize a surfref/texref binding from a non-symbol address, so the correct behavior for this unsupported input is a clean diagnostic rather than an assert/UB. The fix grabs operand 7 once, checks isSymbol(), and calls report_fatal_error (the established NVPTX pattern for unlowerable input, e.g. NVPTXISelDAGToDAG.cpp and NVPTXAsmPrinter.cpp) when it is not a symbol; otherwise it runs the existing replacement unchanged. Added the explicit ErrorHandling.h include for report_fatal_error since it is not clearly pulled in transitively. The x86 oracle is not applicable here: this is a crash in an NVPTX-specific MachineFunction pass, not an AsmPrinter constant/layout bug, and x86 rejects -mcpu=sm_20 / 64-bit NVPTX IR outright.
general_case_safe: The valid common case is unchanged: when the i64 handle is a real surfref/texref kernel parameter (as in test/CodeGen/NVPTX/surf-read.ll), operand 7 is an ExternalSymbol, Addr.isSymbol() is true, and the existing ChangeToES/getImageHandleSymbolIndex path runs exactly as before. The CUDA driver interface still early-returns false before this code. The other branches (texsurf_handles global, COPY/nvvm_move_i64, default) are untouched. The only behavioral change is that an image handle that does not resolve to a parameter symbol now produces a clean fatal diagnostic instead of an assertion abort (debug) or garbage-symbol UB (release).

rationale: The atom address-space qualifier is not a tablegen-visible dimension of these instructions: a single F_ATOMIC_2/F_ATOMIC_3 instruction handles every atom address space, and the '.addsp' sub-qualifier is filled in at selection time by the GetAddSp SDNodeXForm calling getAtomicAddrSpace. So a Requires<[hasClusters]> predicate on the instruction cannot conditionally apply per-address-space (it would wrongly block ALL atoms). The correct chokepoint is the C++ getAtomicAddrSpace, which already centralizes atom-specific address-space validation and already uses report_fatal_error for the unsupported const/local/param spaces. I add the same clean-error treatment for SharedCluster when the subtarget lacks cluster support, using exactly the in-tree floor encoded by hasClusters() (SmVersion>=90 && PTXVersion>=78) — the same predicate the sibling cvta.shared::cluster paths use. getAtomicAddrSpace was static; I make it a const member so it can read Subtarget (like its siblings getMemOrder/getAtomicScope). Both call sites (line ~2304 selection code and the GetAddSp SDNodeXForm body, which is emitted as an ISel member method alongside member helpers getI32Imm/CurDAG) run in NVPTXDAGToDAGISel member context, so the call syntax is unchanged and Subtarget is non-null at selection time. This is C++/header only; no .td edited, so no TableGen rebuild. The result on pre-sm_90 targets is a clear diagnostic instead of invalid PTX; on sm_90+/PTX7.8+ the existing valid .shared::cluster path is taken unchanged.
general_case_safe: The guard fires only for AddressSpace::SharedCluster (numeric AS 7) AND only when Subtarget->hasClusters() is false (SmVersion < 90 || PTXVersion < 78). For sm_90+/PTX7.8+ targets hasClusters() is true, so SharedCluster falls through to 'return AS' exactly as before and valid .shared::cluster atoms still select and emit correctly. Generic/Global/Shared atom address spaces are completely untouched (still returned directly). The pre-existing report_fatal_error path for const/local/param/entryparam/deviceparam is preserved verbatim. Byte/word sizes, orderings, scopes, and the b128 CAS/EXCH path all funnel through this same getAtomicAddrSpace, so they get the identical correct guard. The floor matches the instruction's real minimum architecture, so the only behavior change is: invalid pre-Hopper cluster atoms now produce a clean fatal diagnostic instead of unassemblable PTX.

rationale: The crash is reached only through printModuleLevelGV: for a declaration (no initializer) it calls emitPTXGlobalVariable, which unconditionally queries the value type's preferred alignment and store size. For an opaque/unsized struct type these DataLayout queries assert. emitPTXGlobalVariable has exactly one caller (the declaration path), and the definition path (lines 1032/1081) requires an initializer and is therefore always sized, so the unsized case can only arrive via a declaration. I added an early return in printModuleLevelGV right after the value type is computed and BEFORE any text (the `.extern ` linkage prefix at line 911) is written, so no dangling/partial output is emitted. The guard is `GVar->isDeclaration() && !ETy->isSized()`. An unsized type can only legally appear on a declaration (a definition's initializer forces a sized type per the IR verifier); the explicit isDeclaration() check makes the intent clear and keeps the change conservative. This matches the oracle: x86 emits nothing for a pure external declaration of an unsized global. I placed the check before the texture/surface/sampler opaque-handle branches, but those globals are detected via NVVM metadata and always use sized i64 value types (confirmed in texsurf-queries.ll: `@tex0 = ... global i64 0`), so they are never skipped by this guard.
general_case_safe: Sized external globals are unaffected: `!ETy->isSized()` is false for i32, [4 x i32], vectors, sized structs, etc., so they still take the existing `.extern .global .align N ...` path (verified: `@g = external global i32` still emits `.extern .global .align 4 .u32 g;`). The new branch only fires for declarations whose value type is genuinely unsized (opaque/incomplete), the exact case that has no representable PTX size/alignment — for which emitting nothing is the only correct behavior and matches the target-independent x86 oracle. Texture/surface/sampler opaque-handle globals use sized i64 value types and are identified by metadata, so they are not skipped and their special `.global .texref/.surfref/.samplerref` emission (which comes after this check) is unchanged. The isDeclaration() conjunct guarantees no global with an initializer (definitions, which must be sized) is ever skipped.

rationale: The whole cp.reduce.async.bulk.tensor.* family funnels through SelectCpAsyncBulkTensorReduceCommon (all 8 reduction ops x {tile,im2col} x dims 1..5 x shared32/64 x {plain,_CH}), so a single guard at its entry covers every affected variant. The check Subtarget->getSmVersion() < 90 || Subtarget->getPTXVersion() < 80 is the exact C++ equivalent of the .td Requires<[hasPTX<80>, hasSM<90>]> (hasSM<90> -> getSmVersion() >= 90, hasPTX<80> -> getPTXVersion() >= 80, per NVPTXInstrInfo.td:153-154). I used report_fatal_error rather than silently falling back because there is no legal pre-Hopper expansion for this instruction; this mirrors the established precedent in the same file (SelectTcgen05St at line 2105-2108 does exactly this: 'if (!Subtarget->hasTcgen05InstSupport()) report_fatal_error(...)'). No .td change is needed, so no TableGen rebuild. report_fatal_error and Subtarget are already used throughout this file, so no new includes are required.
general_case_safe: Valid Hopper+ uses are unaffected: when getSmVersion() >= 90 and getPTXVersion() >= 80 the guard is skipped and selection proceeds exactly as before. The threshold exactly matches the instruction's real minimum arch (sm_90 / PTX 8.0) as declared by the existing Requires<> on the records and corroborated by the in-tree test cp-async-bulk-tensor-reduce.ll gating ptxas-verify on sm_90 && isa-8.0. Only targets that cannot legally encode this instruction now hit the error, which is the correct behavior (a clean diagnostic instead of ptxas-rejected PTX). report_fatal_error is the same mechanism the sibling C++-selected tcgen05.st path already uses for the identical 'unsupported on this arch' situation, so this matches surrounding style and does not regress any legal code path.

edits.old_string: bool hasAtomScope() const { return SmVersion >= 60; }

rationale: The buggy site (getAtomicScope at NVPTXISelDAGToDAG.cpp:571) gates on Subtarget->hasAtomScope() and, when it returns false, returns NVPTX::Scope::DefaultDevice, which NVPTXInstPrinter::printAtomicCode prints as no qualifier (the legal unscoped `atom.add.u32`). hasAtomScope() previously checked only `SmVersion >= 60`, missing the PTXVersion requirement. The .cta/.gpu/.sys scope qualifiers on `atom` are a PTX ISA 6.0 feature (verified: `llc -mcpu=sm_60` => `.version 5.0` and emits `atom.sys.add.u32`; `llc -mcpu=sm_60 -mattr=+ptx60` => `.version 6.0` and the scoped form is valid; `llc -mcpu=sm_70` defaults to PTX 6.0 and emits scope). Adding `&& PTXVersion >= 60` exactly mirrors the sibling gate hasMemoryOrdering() (`SmVersion >= 70 && PTXVersion >= 60`) and getMinPTXVersionForSM (sm_60/61/62 -> PTX 5.0, sm_70 -> PTX 6.0). Fixing the predicate corrects all three consistently and keeps the change minimal. I did not touch NVPTXISelDAGToDAG.cpp because the existing `if (!hasAtomScope()) return DefaultDevice;` already does the right thing once the predicate is correct.

Only sm_60/61/62 at their default PTX 5.0 lose the scope qualifier, falling back through getAtomicScope's existing `return NVPTX::Scope::DefaultDevice` to the legal unscoped `atom.add.u32` (printAtomicCode emits nothing for DefaultDevice). This matches how the ordering path already behaves at PTX < 6.0 (hasMemoryOrdering()==false drops ordering/scope, e.g. `load atomic ... syncscope("device")` at sm_60 becomes plain ld.volatile.b32). No byte/layout concern; the change narrows an over-permissive feature predicate to its true minimum PTX ISA, so no valid target regresses and previously-invalid targets now emit correct unscoped PTX.
